newsitem.title: USA: Chinese dissident Wang headed for US - State Dept.
newsitem.headline: Chinese dissident Wang headed for US - State Dept.

text.p: Chinese dissident Wang Xizhe was heading for the United States on Tuesday, the State Department said, but a spokesman refused to say when or where he might arrive, respecting Wang's request for privacy.

Although Wang's wife said earlier that her husband had arrived in the United States, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters: "I can't discuss the details of his case because he has not arrived yet in the United States."

Wang, 46, fled to Hong Kong from his home in China's Guangdong Province last weekend, a few days after Communist authorities in Beijing arrested pro-democracy activist Liu Xiaobo and ordered him to serve three years in a labour camp.
Earlier, the Chinese government accused Wang of crossing the border illegally and said authorities were pursuing those who helped him.
Wang's wife, Su Jiang, said on Tuesday that friends of her husband told her he was safely in the United States.
"They said he was now in a safe place," Su Jiang told Reuters by telephone from her home in Guangzhou in southern China. They did not tell her his exact whereabouts in the United States, she added.
